workspace_id_header.name: X-Workspace-Id
workspace_id_header.description: The numeric ID of the workspace you want to send a message in. This header is only needed when you authenticate with a service-account bearer token (`sa_live_…`). Service accounts work across workspaces, so you must supply this header so we know which workspace to send from. You can omit this header when you authenticate with a standard App API key, which is always scoped to one workspace.

object_type_id.name: object_type_id
object_type_id.description: The object type an object belongs to—like "Companies" or "Accounts". Object type IDs begin at `1` and increment for each new type.

object_id.name: object_id
object_id.description: The `object_id` or `cio_object_id` of an object, depending on the `id_type` specified in query params. `id_type` defaults to `object_id`.

suppression_type.name: suppression_type
suppression_type.description: The reason a person's email address was suppressed by the email service provider (ESP).

transactional_id.name: transactional_id
transactional_id.description: The identifier of your transactional message. You'll find this in the UI or URL of your transactional message. For example, if this is the path of a transactional message URL - `/transactional/3/templates/139` - the `transactional_id` is 3.

delivery_id.name: delivery_id
delivery_id.description: The delivery resulting in a request to unsubscribe.

activityTypes.name: type
activityTypes.description: The type of activity you want to search for. Types with `_o:<object_type_id>` are for objects and types with `_r:<object_type_id>` are for relationships.

schema.description: The type of activity. Types with `_o:<object_type_id>` are for objects and types with `_r:<object_type_id>` are for relationships.

sort.name: sort
sort.description: Determine how you want to sort results, `asc` for chronological order and `desc` for reverse chronological order.

activityName.name: name
activityName.description: The name of the event or attribute you want to return.

deleted.name: deleted
deleted.description: If true, return results for deleted people.

customer_id_query.name: customer_id
customer_id_query.description:
The `identifier` of the person you want to look up. By default, this is a person's `id`. You can use the `id_type` parameter to look up a person by `email`, `phone`, or `cio_id`.

If you use a person's `cio_id`, you must prefix the value with `cio_` when using it to find or reference a person (i.e. `cio_03000010` for a `cio_id` value of 03000010).

id_type.name: id_type
id_type.description: The type of `customer_id` you want to use to reference a person. If you don't provide this parameter, we assume that the `customer_id` in your request is a person's `id`. You can use `email` and `phone` only if they're enabled as identifiers in your [workspace settings](/accounts/workspaces/overview/#migrate-workspace); otherwise the request returns `400`. Reference `phone` values in [E.164 format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.164), like `+14155552671`, and URL-encode the leading `+` as `%2B`.

export_id.name: export_id
export_id.description: The export_id you want to access.

language-1.name: language
language-1.description: A [language tag](/journeys/channels/subscriptions/unsubscribe-faqs/#currently-supported-languages) you want the content translated in. If none is provided, the content will be sent in the default language of your subscription center.

language-2.name: language
language-2.description: A [language tag](/journeys/channels/subscriptions/unsubscribe-faqs/#currently-supported-languages) of a language variant. If you don't provide a language (an empty string), we'll use your default language. If the language variant does not exist, we'll return an error.

newsletter_id.name: newsletter_id
newsletter_id.description: The identifier of a one-time send.

content_id.name: content_id
content_id.description:
The identifier of a message in a one-time send. If your one-time send has an A/B test group or includes multiple languages, each variant has its own `content_id`, separate from the `newsletter_id`.

Use [List variants of a one-time send](/integrations/api/app/tag/newsletter-variants/listNewsletterVariants/) to find the `content_id` associated with the right variant.

campaign_id_query.name: campaign_id
campaign_id_query.description: The automation you want to filter for.

newsletter_id_query.name: newsletter_id
newsletter_id_query.description: The one-time send you want to filter for.

action_id_query.name: action_id
action_id_query.description: The action you want to filter for.

campaign_id.description: The ID of the automation that you want to trigger or return information about.

trigger_id.name: trigger_id
trigger_id.description: The ID of the automation trigger that you want to return information for.

track_customer_id.name: identifier
track_customer_id.description:
The unique value representing a person. The values you use to identify a person may be an `id`, `email` address, or the `cio_id` (when updating people), depending on your workspace settings. When you reference people by `cio_id`, you must prefix the value with `cio_`.

You can't reference a person by their `phone` number here. We determine the identifier type from the shape of the value, so a phone number in the path is treated as an `id`. To identify people by phone number, use the [Track v2 API](/integrations/api/track/tag/track_v2/).

oneOf.title: id
oneOf.description: The unique identifier for a person that you want to create or modify.

oneOf.title: email
oneOf.description: A person's email address. If adding a new person in an email-based workspace, you must use this value.

oneOf.title: cio_id
oneOf.description:
A canonical identifier assigned by Customer.io when you add a person. When referencing a person by this value, you must prefix the value with `cio_`. You can [look up a person using the App API](/integrations/api/app/tag/customers/) to find their `cio_id`.

You must use this value to update a person's other identifiers—their `id` or `email`, unless you enable your workspace's [Allow updates to email using ID](/accounts/workspaces#update-email-with-id) setting.

trackEvent_customer_id.name: identifier
trackEvent_customer_id.description: The unique value representing a person. You may identify a person by `id`, `email` address, or the `cio_id` (when updating people), depending on your workspace settings. You can't reference a person by their `phone` number here; a phone number in the path is treated as an `id`. To identify people by phone number, use the [Track v2 API](/integrations/api/track/tag/track_v2/).

oneOf.title: id
oneOf.description: The unique identifier you assigned to a person.

oneOf.title: cio_id
oneOf.description:
A canonical identifier assigned by Customer.io when you add a person. When referencing a person by this value, you must prefix the value with `cio_`. You can [look up a person using the App API](/integrations/api/app/tag/customers/) to find their `cio_id`, but you must prefix this value with `cio_` when using it to reference a person.

You can use this value to update a person's other identifiers—their `id` or `email`.

device_id.name: device_id
device_id.description: The ID of the device you want to perform an operation against.

segment_id.name: segment_id
segment_id.description: The identifier for a segment. You can find your segment's ID on its page in the dashboard—go to *Segments*, select your segment, and find the ID under *Usage*. Or you can find your segment using the [App API](/integrations/api/app/tag/segments/).

start.description: The token for the page of results you want to return. Responses contain a `next` property. Use this property as the `start` value to return the next page of results.

resolution.name: res
resolution.description: Determines increment for metrics—hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly.

journey_resolution.name: resolution
journey_resolution.description: Determines the increment for journey metrics—hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly.

limit-100-1000.description: The maximum number of results you want to retrieve per page.

action_id.name: action_id
action_id.description: The action you want to lookup or act on.

period.name: period
period.description: The unit of time for your report.

steps.name: steps
steps.description: The number of periods you want to return. Defaults to the maximum available, or `12` if the period is in `months`. Maximums are 24 hours, 45 days, 12 weeks, or 121 months. Days start at 00:00 EST. Weeks start at 00:00 EST on Sunday. Months start at 00:00 EST on the 1st of the month.

metricType.description: The type of item you want to return metrics for. When empty, the response contains metrics for all possible types.

newsletterMetricsType.name: type
newsletterMetricsType.description: The type of item you want to return metrics for. When empty, the response contains metrics for all possible types.

metric.description: Determines the metric(s) you want to return.

unique.name: unique
unique.description: If true, the response contains only unique customer results, i.e. a customer who clicks a link twice is only counted once. If false, the response contains the total number of results without regard to uniqueness.

drafts.name: drafts
drafts.description: If true, your request returns drafts rather than active/sent messages.

get_tracked_responses.name: get_tracked_responses
get_tracked_responses.description: If true, the response includes `tracked_responses` for each message—an object containing tracked response option names for in-app survey responses.

get_apitb_broadcast_id.name: broadcast_id
get_apitb_broadcast_id.description: The ID of the broadcast that you want to return information about.

end_ts.description: The ending timestamp for your query.

AssetParentFolderID.description: Filter results to a specific parent folder. Use 0 or omit to target the root level.

DirectDescendantsOnly.name: direct_descendants_only
DirectDescendantsOnly.description: If true, this returns only children of the parent folder.

email_id.name: id
email_id.description: The UUID of the email. If your email has multiple languages, you must provide the ID of the **default** language template. This links the workflow to all of the language variants for the template.

email_variant_id.name: id
email_variant_id.description: The UUID of the email. If your email has translations, this is the ID of a specific language variant.

inbox_id.name: id
inbox_id.description: The UUID of the inbox message. If the message has multiple languages, you must provide the ID of the **default** language template. This links the workflow to all of the language variants for the template.

run_id.name: run_id
run_id.description: The ID of the inbox preview job, returned by [Send for inbox previews](/integrations/api/app/tag/design-studio-emails/submitInboxPreview/).

preview_client_id.name: client_id
preview_client_id.description: The device identifier for the capture, matching a value from `client_ids` in the response of [Send for inbox previews](/integrations/api/app/tag/design-studio-emails/submitInboxPreview/).

Language.name: language
Language.description: A [language code](/journeys/channels/localization/attribute/#supported-languages) that indicates the language of your translated email

ParentFolderID.name: parent_folder_id
ParentFolderID.description:
Filter by parent folder. Must reference an existing folder. If not set, the response filters by the root level directory.

To list only items in the root folder, leave `parent_folder_id` unset and only set `direct_descendants_only` to `true`.

Their opens, clicks, and bounces count toward your message metrics. CC recipients count toward the limit of 15 total recipients across the `to`, `cc`, and `bcc` keys.

tracked.description: If true, Customer.io tracks opens and link clicks in your message.

app_identifier.description: The app that the device belongs to—the **Bundle ID / App identifier** you entered with that app's push credentials. If you have more than one app, we use this attribute to send push notifications to the right app. A device without an app identifier receives push notifications you send to your [default app](/messaging/channels/push/getting-started/#the-default-app).

app_version.description: The version of your app that a customer uses. You might target app versions to let people know when they need to update, or expose them to new features when they do.

cio_sdk_version.description: The version of the Customer.io SDK in the app.

device_locale.description: The device's [IETF language code](/journeys/channels/localization/getting-started/#supported-languages), such as `en-MX` or `es-ES`.

device_model.description: The model of the device a person uses.

device_os.description: The operating system, including the version, on the device.

push_enabled.description: If `"true"`, the device is opted-in and can receive push notifications.

additionalProperties.description: Custom properties that you want to associate with the device.

last_used.description: The `timestamp` when you last identified this device. If you don't pass a timestamp when you add or update a device, we use the time of the request itself. Our SDKs identify a device when a person launches their app.

custom_payload.description: Optional key/value pairs you want to attach to the push payload. Firebase only supports string values. This overrides all other payload values, including the Custom Payload from your transactional template.

android.description: A custom push payload for Android devices.

message.description: The parent object for Android custom push payloads.

android.description: Contains custom push options for your notification.

notification.description: Properties supported specifically by Android on FCM.

body_loc_arg.description: Variable string values used in place of the format specifiers in `body_loc_key` to localize the body text to the user's current localization. See Formatting and Styling for more information.

body_loc_key.description: String resource key used to localize the body text. See Android [String resources](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/resources/string-resource/).

click_action.description: The action that occurs when a user taps on the notification. Launches an activity with a matching intent filter when a person taps the notification.

color.description: The notification's icon color in `#rrggbb` format.

icon.description: Sets the notification icon to `myicon` for drawable resource `myicon`. If you don't send this key, FCM displays the launcher icon from your app manifest.

sound.description: The sound that plays when the device receives the notification. Supports `"default"` or the filename of a sound resource bundled in your app. Sound files must reside in `/res/raw/`.

tag.description: An identifier you use to replace an existing notification. If a notification with the same tag is already showing, the new one replaces it. Leave it empty to create a new notification each time.

title_loc_arg.description: Variable string values used in place of the format specifiers in `title_loc_key` to localize the title text to the user's current localization. See Formatting and Styling for more information.

type.description: The channel type for the one-time send.

body.description: The HTML body content of the email. Use standard HTML/CSS, not syntax unique to Design Studio.

name.description: The name of the one-time send.

subject.description: The subject line of the email.

body_plain.description: The plaintext body of the email. If provided, this overwrites the auto-generated plaintext.

deduped.description: When `true`, Customer.io sends only one message per email address or phone number, even when several profiles share it. Supported on `email`, `twilio`, and `sms` one-time sends. Leave it out to use the default for your workspace's identifier configuration. No endpoint changes this later, so set it here if you don't want the default.

expires_after.description: A send window in seconds, or `0` for no expiry. Customer.io stops delivering the one-time send once the window closes, so a delayed message doesn't arrive when it's no longer useful. Set it here only alongside `send_now` or `scheduled_at`, because the window runs from the send. On a plain draft, set it on the [send](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/sendNewsletter/) or [schedule](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/scheduleNewsletter/) call instead.

from.description: The address to send the email from, in the format `Name <email@domain.com>`. You can set `from` or `from_id`, but not both. Use one of the `address` values from [List sender identities](/integrations/api/app/tag/sender-identities/listSenders/).

from_id.description: The identifier of the `from` address, commonly known as the "sender". Use [List sender identities](/integrations/api/app/tag/sender-identities/listSenders/) to find valid IDs.

layout_id.description: The ID of the [layout](/journeys/channels/email/layouts/3-layouts-and-customerio/) you want to use for the email. If you don't set one, the email uses your workspace's default layout. Find a layout's ID in its URL.

preheader_text.description: [Also known as "preview text"](/journeys/channels/email/headers/custom-preheader-text/), this is the small block of text shown in an email inbox next to or underneath the subject line.

rate_limit_email_rate.description: Maximum number of messages per time period. **NOTE:** Though this states `email_rate`, you can use this for other message channels. Only fixed rate limits are supported, not [daily ramp limits](/messaging/send/broadcasts/one-time-sends/#daily-ramp).

rate_limit_spread.description: When `true`, spreads messages evenly across the time period. Otherwise, it sends as fast as possible up to the limit in each period.

rate_limit_time_period.description: Time period in seconds for rate limiting. Must be one of 60 (minute), 3600 (hour), or 86400 (day).

recipient_file_url.description: A URL pointing to a CSV of recipients, used instead of the `recipients` filter. Customer.io resolves the file in the background, so this request can't also send or schedule. Poll [Get a one-time send](/integrations/api/app/tag/newsletters/getNewsletters/) until `recipient_file_status` is `done`, then call [send](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/sendNewsletter/) or [schedule](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/scheduleNewsletter/).

recipients.description:
Filter conditions that define the one-time send's recipients. In `recipients`, you can combine `segment` and `attribute` conditions with `and`, `or`, and `not` operators.

This endpoint enforces a strict shape:

* The outermost object must be a single `and` array.
* Every operator or condition object takes exactly **one** key: `and`, `or`, `not`, `segment`, or `attribute`. An object with two keys—like `not` alongside `and`—is rejected with an "Invalid filter spec" error.
* Segment conditions must be wrapped in an `or` array, even for a single segment—and `or` arrays can contain only segment conditions.
* To exclude segments, `not` must contain an `or` of segment conditions and sit as its own item inside the `and` array.
* Attribute conditions sit directly in the `and` array, unwrapped. To negate an attribute condition, set `inverse: true` on the attribute itself—`not` can't contain attribute conditions.

The email example on this operation shows or-wrapped segments combined with a negated attribute; for the common "include segment A, exclude segment B" pattern, see the **include one segment, exclude another** request example. See [Format API-triggered broadcasts](/messaging/send/broadcasts/api-triggered-data-format/#overriding-recipients) for general operator behavior.

and.description: An array of conditions that must all be true.

field.description: The attribute name.

inverse.description: Set to `true` for "is not equal" or "does not exist".

operator.description: The comparison operator.

value.description: The value to compare against. Required when `operator` is `eq`.

not.description: A condition or group of conditions to exclude. On this endpoint, `not` must contain an `or` of segment conditions and sit as its own item inside the `and` array. An object with both `and` and `not` keys is rejected with an "Invalid filter spec" error.

or.description: An array of conditions where at least one must be true. On this endpoint, `or` arrays can contain only segment conditions.

segment.description: A segment condition.

id.description: The ID of a segment.

scheduled_at.description: A Unix timestamp indicating when to send the one-time send. The time must be in the future. You cannot set both `send_now` and `scheduled_at`.

send_now.description: If `true`, the one-time send is sent immediately after creation. You cannot set both `send_now` and `scheduled_at`.

subscription_topic_id.description: The one-time send audience's subscription topic ID. Required when [subscription center](/journeys/channels/subscriptions/center/#enable-sub-center) is enabled; otherwise sends to globally subscribed profiles.

tag_ids.description: The IDs of the tags you want to apply to the one-time send. Each tag must already exist.

body_json.description:
JSON body content for the in-app message, as a stringified JSON object—a JSON string, not a nested object. It supports these fields:
- `message_id`—string, an identifier for the message
- `carta_content`—string, the message content markup from our in-app editor
- `display`—object; `mode` (`modal`, `overlay`, `inline`, or `tooltip`) and `value` (the position for modals: `top`, `center`, or `bottom`; the position ID for inline messages). Tooltips take a `tooltip_target` CSS selector instead of `value`
- `priority`—integer, delivery order for queued messages: `1` (low), `5` (medium), or `10` (high)
- `expiration`—object; if omitted, the message expires after 30 days (60 maximum). Set `type` (`relative` or `absolute`), `unit`, and `value`
- `persistent`—boolean, keep the message visible across pages and sessions until your audience dismisses it
- `attributes`—object, custom key-value string pairs delivered with the message
- `route_rules` and `excluded_route_rules`—objects keyed by platform (`web`, `ios`, or `android`), each holding an array of [page rules](/messaging/channels/in-app/send-in-app-message/#page-rule) with an `operator` (`contains` or `equals`), a `value` (`*` is a wildcard), and an `order` (integer). You can only set page rules when you create a message, and platforms you don't set rules for won't show the message

newsletterRateLimitOptions.description: Optional one-time send rate limiting. If you set `rate_limit_email_rate` or `rate_limit_time_period`, set both; `rate_limit_spread` can be set alone.

rate_limit_email_rate.description: Maximum number of messages per time period. **NOTE:** Though this states `email_rate`, you can use this for other message channels. Only fixed rate limits are supported, not [daily ramp limits](/messaging/send/broadcasts/one-time-sends/#daily-ramp).

rate_limit_spread.description: When `true`, spreads messages evenly across the time period. Otherwise, it sends as fast as possible up to the limit in each period.

rate_limit_time_period.description: Time period in seconds for rate limiting. Must be one of 60 (minute), 3600 (hour), or 86400 (day).

allOf.description: Optional one-time send rate limiting. If you set `rate_limit_email_rate` or `rate_limit_time_period`, set both; `rate_limit_spread` can be set alone.

scheduled_at.description: Unix timestamp for the send. Use `0` to deschedule. When greater than `0`, the time must be in the future and you must send `timezone` so the UI displays the time correctly.

expires_after.description: A send window in seconds measured from the scheduled time, or `0` for no expiry. Customer.io stops delivering the one-time send once the window closes. You can't combine it with `tz_match_enabled`, with send time optimization, or with descheduling (`scheduled_at` of `0`), and on an A/B test it must outlast the test duration.

rate_limit_email_rate.description: Maximum number of messages per time period. **NOTE:** Though this states `email_rate`, you can use this for other message channels. Only fixed rate limits are supported, not [daily ramp limits](/messaging/send/broadcasts/one-time-sends/#daily-ramp).

rate_limit_spread.description: When `true`, spreads messages evenly across the time period. Otherwise, it sends as fast as possible up to the limit in each period.

rate_limit_time_period.description: Time period in seconds for rate limiting. Must be one of 60 (minute), 3600 (hour), or 86400 (day).

timezone.description: [IANA timezone name](/journeys/send/timezones/example-timezones/#region-format) (for example, `America/New_York`). Required when `scheduled_at` is greater than `0`. Not required when descheduling (`scheduled_at` is `0`).

tz_match_enabled.description: When `true`, sends at the same local time in each recipient's timezone. If it's set to `true` and `rate_limit_time_period` is provided, then the period can't be greater than `3600` (1 hour).

content_ids.description: A list of message variants in a one-time send, where a variant is a translation or A/B test.

created.description: The date time when the referenced ID was created.

deduplicate_id.description: An identifier in the format `id:timestamp` where the id is for the object you're working with (Automations, Deliveries, Exports, Identities, One-time sends, Segments, and Templates), and the timestamp is the last time the object was updated.

expires_after.description: The send window in seconds, if you set one. Customer.io stops delivering the one-time send this long after it starts.

id.description: The identifier for a one-time send.

name.description: The name of the one-time send. Must be 190 characters or less.

recipient_file_error.description: Why the recipient file failed, when `recipient_file_status` is `error`. Customer.io omits it otherwise.

recipient_file_status.description: How far Customer.io has got with a recipient file, whether you uploaded it in the UI or passed `recipient_file_url`. Customer.io omits this field when the audience came from a `recipients` filter. Wait for `done` before you send or schedule.

recipient_segment_ids.description: If the recipient conditions included segments, this returns a list of those segment ids.

sent_at.description: The last time the one-time send was sent.

subscription_topic_id.description: If you enabled a [subscription center](/journeys/channels/subscriptions/center/) on your workspace, this returns the id of the subscription preference you set.

tags.description: An array of tags associated with the one-time send.

type.description: Channel type for a one-time send or one-time send content variant.

updated.description: The date time when the referenced ID was last updated.

customer_events.description: Describes the customer events reported from Customer.io to a webhook.

customer_subscribed.description: A person's `unsubscribed` attribute was explicitly set to `false`. Set to true to report `subscribed` events.

customer_subscription_preferences_change.description: A person's subscription preferences changed. [Learn more about the subscription center](/journeys/channels/subscriptions/center/).

customer_unsubscribed.description: A person's `unsubscribed` attribute was explicitly set to `true`. Set to true to report `unsubscribed` events.

email_events.description: Describes the email events reported from Customer.io to a webhook.

email_attempted.description: Reports when a message cannot be sent to the delivery provider and will retry. Set to true to report this event type.

email_bounced.description: Reports when the delivery provider is unable to deliver a message. Set to true to report this event type.

email_clicked.description: Reports when a person clicks a tracked link in a message. Set to true to report this event type.

email_converted.description: Reports a conversion. Set to true to report this event type.

email_deferred.description: Reports when the delivery provider couldn't send a message and will retry. Set to true to report this event type.

email_delivered.description: Reports when the delivery provider reports that a message is delivered to an inbox. Set to true to report this event type.

email_drafted.description: Reports when a message draft is created. Set to true to report this event type.

email_dropped.description: Reports when a message isn't sent because the recipient is suppressed. Set to true to report this event type.

email_failed.description: Reports when an email couldn't be sent to the delivery provider. Set to true to report this event type.

email_opened.description: Reports when a recipient opens a message. Set to true to report this event type.

email_sent.description: Reports when a message is sent from Customer.io to the delivery provider. Set to true to report this event type.

email_spammed.description: Reports a recipient marks a message as spam. Set to true to report this even type.

email_unsubscribed.description: Reports when a person unsubscribes through a particular email. Set to true to report this event type.

push_events.description: Describes the push events reported from Customer.io to a webhook.

push_attempted.description: Reports when a push notification could not be sent to the delivery provider will retry. Set to true to report this event type.

push_bounced.description: Reports when the delivery provider is unable to deliver a message. Set to true to report this event type.

push_clicked.description: Reports when a person clicks a tracked link in a message. Set to true to report this event type.

push_converted.description: Reports a conversion. Set to true to report this event type.

push_delivered.description: An app reports that the recipient's device received a message. Set to true to report this event type.

push_drafted.description: Reports when a message draft is created. Set to true to report this event type.

push_dropped.description: Reports when a message isn't sent because the recipient is suppressed. Set to true to report this event type.

push_failed.description: Reports when a message couldn't be sent to the delivery provider. Set to true to report this event type.

push_opened.description: The app on a recipient's device reports that the recipient opened the message. Set to true to report this event type.

push_sent.description: Reports when a message is sent from Customer.io to the delivery provider. Set to true to report this event type.

sms_events.description: Describes the SMS events reported from Customer.io to a webhook.

sms_attempted.description: Reports when a push notification could not be sent to the delivery provider will retry. Set to true to report this event type.

sms_bounced.description: Reports when the delivery provider is unable to deliver a message to the recipient. Set to true to report this event type.

sms_clicked.description: Reports when a person clicks a tracked link in a message. Set to true to report this event type.

sms_converted.description: Reports when a person matches conversion criteria attributed to a a message. Set to true to report this event type.

sms_delivered.description: The delivery provider reports that the message is delivered. Set to true to report this event type.

sms_drafted.description: Reports when a message draft is created. Set to true to report this event type.

sms_dropped.description: Reports when a message isn't sent because the recipient opted out or their phone number can't receive SMS. Set to true to report this event type.

sms_failed.description: Reports when a message couldn't be sent to the delivery provider. Set to true to report this event type.

sms_sent.description: Reports when a message is sent from Customer.io to the delivery provider. Set to true to report this event type.

slack_events.description: Describes the slack events reported from Customer.io to a webhook.

slack_attempted.description: Reports when a message could not be sent to the delivery provider will retry. Set to true to report this event type.

slack_clicked.description: Reports when a person clicks a tracked link in a message. Set to true to report this event type.

slack_converted.description: Reports when a person matches conversion criteria attributed to a a message. Set to true to report this event type.

slack_drafted.description: Reports when a message draft is created. Set to true to report this event type.

slack_failed.description: Reports when a message couldn't be sent to the delivery provider. Set to true to report this event type.

slack_sent.description: Reports when a message is sent from Customer.io to the delivery provider. Set to true to report this event type.

webhook_events.description: Describes the webhook events reported from Customer.io to a webhook.

webhook_attempted.description: Reports when a webhook could not be sent and will retry. Set to true to report this event type.

webhook_clicked.description: Reports when a tracked link in a webhook payload is opened. Set to true to report this event type.

webhook_drafted.description: A webhook draft is created. Set to true to report this event type.

webhook_failed.description: Reports when a webhook couldn't be sent to the webhook URL. Set to true to report this event type.

webhook_sent.description: Reports when a webhook is sent from Customer.io to the webhook URL. Set to true to report this event type.

body_content.description: Message content in reporting webhooks when Body Content is enabled and the metric is `sent`. Email content includes headers; push and in-app content is stringified payload.

events.description: Specifies the types of events you want to report to your webhook. See our [reporting webhooks reference](/integrations/api/webhooks/) for more information about event types and the information they return.

name.description: The name of your webhook.

disabled.description: Set to `true` to quit sending events to the webhook URL. Set to `false` to enable the webhook.

full_resolution.description: Set to `false` to send unique open and click events to the webhook. Set to `true` to send all events.

id.description: The identifier for the webhook.

type.description: The type of webhook—`webhook` for a standard reporting webhook or `js` for a JavaScript webhook.

with_content.description: Set to `true` to include the message `body` in `_sent` events.

url.description: The URL of a webhook or action.

request_method.description: The method used in conjunction with a webhook `url`.

forgotten.description: If true, Customer.io does not retain the message content.

archivedMessageObject.description: An archived message, including a complete message body.

bcc.description: The blind-copy address(es) for this action.

body.description: The body of the variant. You cannot modify the body if you created it with our drag-and-drop editor.

cc.description: The carbon-copy address(es) for this action.

fake_bcc.description: If true, rather than sending true copies to BCC addresses, Customer.io sends a copy of the message with the subject line containing the recipient address(es).

forgotten.description: If true, Customer.io does not retain the message content.

from.description: The address that the message is from, relevant if the action `type` is `email`.

headers.description: A JSON string containing header objects with `name` and `value`. Names and values must be strings, with no non-ASCII characters or spaces. You can't overwrite reserved headers.

id.description: The identifier for a delivery—the instance of a message intended for an individual recipient.

preheader_text.description: [Also known as "preview text"](/journeys/channels/email/headers/custom-preheader-text/), this is the small block of text shown in an email inbox next to or underneath the subject line.

recipient.description: The recipient address for an action.

reply_to.description: The address that receives replies for the message, if applicable.

request_method.description: The method used in conjunction with a webhook `url`.

subject.description: The subject line for an `email` action.
subject.example: Did you get that thing I sent you?

phone.description: The person's phone number. This key only appears if your workspace has phone enabled as an identifier.

trigger_id.description: The trigger ID returned by the [Trigger Broadcast API](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/triggerBroadcast/).

broadcast_name.description: The name of the broadcast. Omitted when the name isn't available—for example, if the broadcast was deleted.

broadcast_tags.description: The tags on the broadcast, as an array of tag names. Omitted when the broadcast has no tags or the tags aren't available.

customer_id.description:
The ID of the person the webhook event occurred to. Blank if the person in question has been deleted.

While webhooks may still contain this property, you should rely on the newer `identifiers` object wherever possible.

journey_id.description: The ID for the path a person went through in an automation or API Triggered Broadcast workflow.

parent_action_id.description: The ID of the parent action, if the action occurred within an automation and has a parent (like a randomized split, etc).

template_id.description: The ID of the template used to render the message. A message's content can change over its lifetime; this is the template used for this delivery. For one-time sends (newsletters), this matches `content_id`.

delivery_id.description: The instance of a message sent to a person.

identifiers.description:
The person the event represents. This object contains all of the identifiers enabled in your workspace, even if they aren't set for the person. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

phone.description: The person's phone number. This key only appears if your workspace has phone enabled as an identifier.

oneOf.description: The identifier for a one-time send.

identifiers.description:
The person the event represents. This object contains all of the identifiers enabled in your workspace, even if they aren't set for the person. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

identifiers.description:
The person the event represents. This object contains all of the identifiers enabled in your workspace, even if they aren't set for the person. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

customer_id.description:

identifiers.description:
The person the event represents. This object contains all of the identifiers enabled in your workspace, even if they aren't set for the person. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

metric.description: An SMS notification was drafted.

delivery_id.description: The instance of a message sent to a person.

identifiers.description:
The person the event represents. This object contains all of the identifiers enabled in your workspace, even if they aren't set for the person. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

id.description: The ID of a customer profile, analogous to a "person" in the UI. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID), this value can be null.

cio_id.description: The canonical identifier for a person, present only if your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID). This value exists to keep a record of a person in your workspace across changes to their other identifiers.

email.description: The email address of the customer.

phone.description: The person's phone number. This key only appears if your workspace has phone enabled as an identifier.

trigger_id.description: The trigger ID returned by the [Trigger Broadcast API](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/triggerBroadcast/).

broadcast_name.description: The name of the broadcast. Omitted when the name isn't available—for example, if the broadcast was deleted.

broadcast_tags.description: The tags on the broadcast, as an array of tag names. Omitted when the broadcast has no tags or the tags aren't available.

customer_id.description:
The ID of the person the webhook event occurred to. Blank if the person in question has been deleted.

While webhooks may still contain this property, you should rely on the newer `identifiers` object wherever possible.

journey_id.description: The ID for the path a person went through in an automation or API Triggered Broadcast workflow.

parent_action_id.description: The ID of the parent action, if the action occurred within an automation and has a parent (like a randomized split, etc).

template_id.description: The ID of the template used to render the message. A message's content can change over its lifetime; this is the template used for this delivery. For one-time sends (newsletters), this matches `content_id`.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

id.description: The ID of a customer profile, analogous to a "person" in the UI. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID), this value can be null.

cio_id.description: The canonical identifier for a person, present only if your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID). This value exists to keep a record of a person in your workspace across changes to their other identifiers.

email.description: The email address of the customer.

phone.description: The person's phone number. This key only appears if your workspace has phone enabled as an identifier.

oneOf.description: The identifier for a one-time send.

content_id.description: The identifier for a one-time send variant.

customer_id.description:
The ID of the person the webhook event occurred to. Blank if the person in question has been deleted.

While webhooks may still contain this property, you should rely on the newer `identifiers` object wherever possible.

newsletter_name.description: The name of the one-time send. Omitted when the name isn't available—for example, if the one-time send was deleted.

newsletter_tags.description: The tags on the one-time send, as an array of tag names. Omitted when the one-time send has no tags or the tags aren't available.

template_id.description: The ID of the template used to render the message. A message's content can change over its lifetime; this is the template used for this delivery. For one-time sends (newsletters), this matches `content_id`.

href.description: The URL of the link that a person clicked.

link_id.description: The identifier for the tracked link that a person clicked or tapped.

recipient.description: The phone number of the WhatsApp recipient.

event_id.description: The unique ID of the reporting webhook event being sent.

object_type.description: The event relates to a WhatsApp message.

timestamp.description: The unix timestamp when the event occurred.

metric.description: A person matched conversion criteria attributed to a WhatsApp message.

data.description: Contains information about the event, specific to the `object_type` and `metric`.

phone.description: The person's phone number. This key only appears if your workspace has phone enabled as an identifier.

campaign_tags.description: The tags on the automation, as an array of tag names. Omitted when the automation has no tags or the tags aren't available.

customer_id.description:
The ID of the person the webhook event occurred to. Blank if the person in question has been deleted.

While webhooks may still contain this property, you should rely on the newer `identifiers` object wherever possible.

journey_id.description: The ID for the path a person went through in an automation or API Triggered Broadcast workflow.

parent_action_id.description: The ID of the parent action, if the action occurred within an automation and has a parent (like a randomized split, etc).

template_id.description: The ID of the template used to render the message. A message's content can change over its lifetime; this is the template used for this delivery. For one-time sends (newsletters), this matches `content_id`.

trigger_event_id.description: The id of the event that triggered an event-triggered automation (not an API-triggered broadcast).

delivery_id.description: The instance of a message sent to a person.

identifiers.description:
The person the event represents. This object contains all of the identifiers enabled in your workspace, even if they aren't set for the person. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

subject.description: The subject of the email.

machine.description: If true, the click was generated by a machine.

event_id.description: The unique ID of the reporting webhook event being sent.

metric.description: A tracked link in an email was clicked.

object_type.description: The event relates to an email action.

timestamp.description: The unix timestamp when the event occurred.

data.description: Contains information about the event, specific to the `object_type` and `metric`.

delivery_id.description: The instance of a message sent to a person.

identifiers.description:
The person the event represents. This object contains all of the identifiers enabled in your workspace, even if they aren't set for the person. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

id.description: The ID of a customer profile, analogous to a "person" in the UI. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID), this value can be null.

cio_id.description: The canonical identifier for a person, present only if your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID). This value exists to keep a record of a person in your workspace across changes to their other identifiers.

email.description: The email address of the customer.

phone.description: The person's phone number. This key only appears if your workspace has phone enabled as an identifier.

trigger_id.description: The trigger ID returned by the [Trigger Broadcast API](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/triggerBroadcast/).

broadcast_name.description: The name of the broadcast. Omitted when the name isn't available—for example, if the broadcast was deleted.

broadcast_tags.description: The tags on the broadcast, as an array of tag names. Omitted when the broadcast has no tags or the tags aren't available.

customer_id.description:
The ID of the person the webhook event occurred to. Blank if the person in question has been deleted.

While webhooks may still contain this property, you should rely on the newer `identifiers` object wherever possible.

parent_action_id.description: The ID of the parent action, if the action occurred within an automation and has a parent (like a randomized split, etc).

template_id.description: The ID of the template used to render the message. A message's content can change over its lifetime; this is the template used for this delivery. For one-time sends (newsletters), this matches `content_id`.

The person the event represents. This object contains all of the identifiers enabled in your workspace, even if they aren't set for the person. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

id.description: The ID of a customer profile, analogous to a "person" in the UI. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID), this value can be null.

cio_id.description: The canonical identifier for a person, present only if your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID). This value exists to keep a record of a person in your workspace across changes to their other identifiers.

email.description: The email address of the customer.

phone.description: The person's phone number. This key only appears if your workspace has phone enabled as an identifier.

campaign_tags.description: The tags on the automation, as an array of tag names. Omitted when the automation has no tags or the tags aren't available.

customer_id.description:
The ID of the person the webhook event occurred to. Blank if the person in question has been deleted.

While webhooks may still contain this property, you should rely on the newer `identifiers` object wherever possible.

template_id.description: The ID of the template used to render the message. A message's content can change over its lifetime; this is the template used for this delivery. For one-time sends (newsletters), this matches `content_id`.

phone.description: The person's phone number. This key only appears if your workspace has phone enabled as an identifier.

trigger_id.description: The trigger ID returned by the [Trigger Broadcast API](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/triggerBroadcast/).

broadcast_name.description: The name of the broadcast. Omitted when the name isn't available—for example, if the broadcast was deleted.

broadcast_tags.description: The tags on the broadcast, as an array of tag names. Omitted when the broadcast has no tags or the tags aren't available.

customer_id.description:
The ID of the person the webhook event occurred to. Blank if the person in question has been deleted.

While webhooks may still contain this property, you should rely on the newer `identifiers` object wherever possible.

journey_id.description: The ID for the path a person went through in an automation or API Triggered Broadcast workflow.

parent_action_id.description: The ID of the parent action, if the action occurred within an automation and has a parent (like a randomized split, etc).

template_id.description: The ID of the template used to render the message. A message's content can change over its lifetime; this is the template used for this delivery. For one-time sends (newsletters), this matches `content_id`.

delivery_id.description: The instance of a message sent to a person.

identifiers.description:
The person the event represents. This object contains all of the identifiers enabled in your workspace, even if they aren't set for the person. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

The person the event represents. This object contains all of the identifiers enabled in your workspace, even if they aren't set for the person. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

id.description: The ID of a customer profile, analogous to a "person" in the UI. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID), this value can be null.

cio_id.description: The canonical identifier for a person, present only if your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID). This value exists to keep a record of a person in your workspace across changes to their other identifiers.

email.description: The email address of the customer.

phone.description: The person's phone number. This key only appears if your workspace has phone enabled as an identifier.

oneOf.description: The identifier for a one-time send.

content_id.description: The identifier for a one-time send variant.

customer_id.description:
The ID of the person the webhook event occurred to. Blank if the person in question has been deleted.

While webhooks may still contain this property, you should rely on the newer `identifiers` object wherever possible.

newsletter_name.description: The name of the one-time send. Omitted when the name isn't available—for example, if the one-time send was deleted.

newsletter_tags.description: The tags on the one-time send, as an array of tag names. Omitted when the one-time send has no tags or the tags aren't available.

template_id.description: The ID of the template used to render the message. A message's content can change over its lifetime; this is the template used for this delivery. For one-time sends (newsletters), this matches `content_id`.

identifiers.description:
The person the event represents. This object contains all of the identifiers enabled in your workspace, even if they aren't set for the person. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

id.description: The ID of a customer profile, analogous to a "person" in the UI. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID), this value can be null.

cio_id.description: The canonical identifier for a person, present only if your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID). This value exists to keep a record of a person in your workspace across changes to their other identifiers.

email.description: The email address of the customer.

phone.description: The person's phone number. This key only appears if your workspace has phone enabled as an identifier.

trigger_id.description: The trigger ID returned by the [Trigger Broadcast API](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/triggerBroadcast/).

broadcast_name.description: The name of the broadcast. Omitted when the name isn't available—for example, if the broadcast was deleted.

broadcast_tags.description: The tags on the broadcast, as an array of tag names. Omitted when the broadcast has no tags or the tags aren't available.

customer_id.description:
The ID of the person the webhook event occurred to. Blank if the person in question has been deleted.

While webhooks may still contain this property, you should rely on the newer `identifiers` object wherever possible.

journey_id.description: The ID for the path a person went through in an automation or API Triggered Broadcast workflow.

parent_action_id.description: The ID of the parent action, if the action occurred within an automation and has a parent (like a randomized split, etc).

template_id.description: The ID of the template used to render the message. A message's content can change over its lifetime; this is the template used for this delivery. For one-time sends (newsletters), this matches `content_id`.

If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

id.description: The ID of a customer profile, analogous to a "person" in the UI. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID), this value can be null.

cio_id.description: The canonical identifier for a person, present only if your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID). This value exists to keep a record of a person in your workspace across changes to their other identifiers.

email.description: The email address of the customer.

phone.description: The person's phone number. This key only appears if your workspace has phone enabled as an identifier.

campaign_tags.description: The tags on the automation, as an array of tag names. Omitted when the automation has no tags or the tags aren't available.

customer_id.description:
The ID of the person the webhook event occurred to. Blank if the person in question has been deleted.

While webhooks may still contain this property, you should rely on the newer `identifiers` object wherever possible.

journey_id.description: The ID for the path a person went through in an automation or API Triggered Broadcast workflow.

parent_action_id.description: The ID of the parent action, if the action occurred within an automation and has a parent (like a randomized split, etc).

template_id.description: The ID of the template used to render the message. A message's content can change over its lifetime; this is the template used for this delivery. For one-time sends (newsletters), this matches `content_id`.

trigger_event_id.description: The id of the event that triggered an event-triggered automation (not an API-triggered broadcast).

The person the event represents. This object contains all of the identifiers enabled in your workspace, even if they aren't set for the person. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

cio_id.description: The canonical identifier for a person, present only if your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID). This value exists to keep a record of a person in your workspace across changes to their other identifiers.

email.description: The email address of the customer.

phone.description: The person's phone number. This key only appears if your workspace has phone enabled as an identifier.

campaign_tags.description: The tags on the automation, as an array of tag names. Omitted when the automation has no tags or the tags aren't available.

customer_id.description:

phone.description: The person's phone number. This key only appears if your workspace has phone enabled as an identifier.

trigger_id.description: The trigger ID returned by the [Trigger Broadcast API](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/triggerBroadcast/).

broadcast_name.description: The name of the broadcast. Omitted when the name isn't available—for example, if the broadcast was deleted.

broadcast_tags.description: The tags on the broadcast, as an array of tag names. Omitted when the broadcast has no tags or the tags aren't available.

customer_id.description:
The ID of the person the webhook event occurred to. Blank if the person in question has been deleted.

While webhooks may still contain this property, you should rely on the newer `identifiers` object wherever possible.

journey_id.description: The ID for the path a person went through in an automation or API Triggered Broadcast workflow.

parent_action_id.description: The ID of the parent action, if the action occurred within an automation and has a parent (like a randomized split, etc).

template_id.description: The ID of the template used to render the message. A message's content can change over its lifetime; this is the template used for this delivery. For one-time sends (newsletters), this matches `content_id`.

delivery_id.description: The instance of a message sent to a person.

identifiers.description:
The person the event represents. This object contains all of the identifiers enabled in your workspace, even if they aren't set for the person. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

identifiers.description:
The person the event represents. This object contains all of the identifiers enabled in your workspace, even if they aren't set for the person. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

identifiers.description:
The person the event represents. This object contains all of the identifiers enabled in your workspace, even if they aren't set for the person. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

email.description: The email address of the customer.

phone.description: The person's phone number. This key only appears if your workspace has phone enabled as an identifier.

accessibility.description: Applies a set of accessibility improvements to the email HTML. When no `language` is set, this falls back to the `lang` attribute on the `<html>` tag, or `"und"` (undetermined). The `dir` attribute is automatically derived from the language using RTL detection.

add_dir_to_content.description: Add `dir` attribute to direct children of `<body>`.

add_dir_to_html.description: Add `dir` attribute (`ltr`, `rtl`, or `auto`) to the `<html>` element if not already present.

add_empty_alt_to_images.description: Add `alt=""` to `` elements missing an `alt` attribute, preventing screen readers from reading the file name.

add_lang_to_content.description: Add `lang` attribute to direct children of `<body>`.

add_lang_to_html.description: Add `lang` attribute to the `<html>` element if not already present.

add_role_to_tables.description: Add `role="presentation"` to all `<table>` elements without an existing `role`, so screen readers skip table semantics for layout tables.

add_title_to_head.description: Add a `<title>` tag to `<head>` using the email subject line (creates or replaces if empty).

add_vml_alt_text.description: Add `alt` attribute to VML elements (used by Outlook’s Word rendering engine), derived from the element’s text content.

language.description: Language code (for example, `"en"`, `"fr"`, or `"ar"`) used for `lang` and `dir` attributes.

remove_button_role_from_links.description: Remove `role="button"` from `<a>` tags to restore proper link semantics for screen readers.

remove_zoom_meta_tag.description: Remove viewport `<meta>` tags that restrict zoom (`user-scalable=0`, `user-scalable=no`, `maximum-scale=1`, or `maximum-scale=2`).

css_inliner.description: Moves CSS from `<style>` tags into inline `style` attributes on each element. Essential for email clients with limited `<style>` support (for example, older Gmail and some Outlook versions). Uses the `juice` library. Elements in `<style>` tags marked with `data-ignore-inlining` are skipped.

apply_html_attributes.description: Controls adding redundant HTML attributes alongside inlined CSS to different HTML elements.

apply_height_attributes.description:
Add redundant HTML `height` attributes alongside inlined CSS `height` on ``, `
`, ``, and `` elements. Only applies to `px` values (and `%` on table elements). Needed for email clients that ignore CSS height.

apply_table_element_attributes.description: Add redundant HTML attributes on table elements (`<table>`, `<th>`, `<tr>`, `<td>`, `<caption>`, `<colgroup>`, `<col>`, `<thead>`, `<tbody>`, `<tfoot>`): `background-color` → `bgcolor`, `background-image` → `background`, `text-align` → `align`, `vertical-align` → `valign`.

apply_width_attributes.description:
Add redundant HTML `width` attributes alongside inlined CSS `width` on ``, `
`, ``, and `` elements. Only applies to `px` values (and `%` on table elements). Needed for email clients that ignore CSS width (for example, older Outlook).

preserve_pseudos.description: Keep pseudo-selector rules (for example, `:hover`) in `<style>` (cannot be inlined).

remove_style_tags.description: Remove `<style>` tags after inlining their rules.

css_variables.description: Resolves CSS custom properties (`var(--name)`) into their computed values. Required for email clients that do not support CSS custom properties (most email clients). Variables declared in one `<style>` tag are available in subsequent `<style>` tags.

preserve.description: Keep original custom property declarations (`--name: value`) alongside the resolved values.

encode_entities.description: Encodes special characters (for example, `©`, `™`, and `—`) as their HTML entity equivalents. Improves rendering consistency across email clients with varying character encoding support. Only processes text nodes in the `<body>` and skips `<script>`, `<style>`, `<noscript>`, `<svg>`, and `<head>` elements. Preserves Liquid template tags and avoids double-encoding existing entities.

formatter.description: Controls the output formatting of the final HTML. Only one mode (`prettify` or `minify`) can be active at a time. Set to `"none"` to skip formatting entirely.

minify.description: Options used when `type` is `"minify"`. Reduces file size by stripping whitespace and comments.

line_length_limit.description: Maximum characters per line before inserting a line break.

remove_html_comments.description: HTML comment removal level. `"0"` keeps all comments, `"1"` removes non-conditional comments (preserves MSO conditionals like `<!--[if mso]>`), and `"2"` removes all comments including conditional.

remove_line_breaks.description: Remove all line breaks from the output.

prettify.description: Options used when `type` is `"prettify"`. Produces human-readable, indented HTML output.

indent_size.description: Number of indent characters per level.

wrap_attributes.description: Wrap HTML attributes onto separate lines (`force-expand-multiline` mode).

type.description: Formatting mode to apply.

prevent_widows.description: Replaces the last space in text blocks with a non-breaking space (` `) to prevent a single word from wrapping onto its own line (a “widow”). Only processes text nodes in the `<body>` and skips `<script>`, `<style>`, `<noscript>`, `<svg>`, and `<head>` elements. Preserves Liquid template tags (`{{ }} ` and `{% %}`).

remove_unused_css.description: Scans the HTML and removes any CSS selectors from `<style>` tags that are not referenced in the document. Reduces file size and helps avoid Gmail’s 102 KB clipping limit. HTML and CSS comments are always preserved by this step (comment removal is handled separately by the formatter object).

backend_markers.description: Template syntax delimiters (e.g., Liquid, Handlebars) that the CSS parser should skip over to avoid treating template expressions as invalid CSS.

uglify.description: Shorten (uglify) CSS class names to reduce file size.

add_empty_alt_to_images.description: Add `alt=""` to `` elements missing an `alt` attribute, preventing screen readers from reading the file name.

add_lang_to_content.description: Add `lang` attribute to direct children of `<body>`.

add_lang_to_html.description: Add `lang` attribute to the `<html>` element if not already present.

add_role_to_tables.description: Add `role="presentation"` to all `<table>` elements without an existing `role`, so screen readers skip table semantics for layout tables.

add_title_to_head.description: Add a `<title>` tag to `<head>` using the email subject line (creates or replaces if empty).

add_vml_alt_text.description: Add `alt` attribute to VML elements (used by Outlook’s Word rendering engine), derived from the element’s text content.

language.description: Language code (for example, `"en"`, `"fr"`, or `"ar"`) used for `lang` and `dir` attributes.

remove_button_role_from_links.description: Remove `role="button"` from `<a>` tags to restore proper link semantics for screen readers.

remove_zoom_meta_tag.description: Remove viewport `<meta>` tags that restrict zoom (`user-scalable=0`, `user-scalable=no`, `maximum-scale=1`, or `maximum-scale=2`).

css_inliner.description: Moves CSS from `<style>` tags into inline `style` attributes on each element. Essential for email clients with limited `<style>` support (for example, older Gmail and some Outlook versions). Uses the `juice` library. Elements in `<style>` tags marked with `data-ignore-inlining` are skipped.

apply_html_attributes.description: Controls adding redundant HTML attributes alongside inlined CSS to different HTML elements.

apply_height_attributes.description:
Add redundant HTML `height` attributes alongside inlined CSS `height` on ``, `
`, ``, and `` elements. Only applies to `px` values (and `%` on table elements). Needed for email clients that ignore CSS height.

apply_table_element_attributes.description: Add redundant HTML attributes on table elements (`<table>`, `<th>`, `<tr>`, `<td>`, `<caption>`, `<colgroup>`, `<col>`, `<thead>`, `<tbody>`, `<tfoot>`): `background-color` → `bgcolor`, `background-image` → `background`, `text-align` → `align`, `vertical-align` → `valign`.

apply_width_attributes.description:
Add redundant HTML `width` attributes alongside inlined CSS `width` on ``, `
`, ``, and `` elements. Only applies to `px` values (and `%` on table elements). Needed for email clients that ignore CSS width (for example, older Outlook).

preserve_pseudos.description: Keep pseudo-selector rules (for example, `:hover`) in `<style>` (cannot be inlined).

remove_style_tags.description: Remove `<style>` tags after inlining their rules.

css_variables.description: Resolves CSS custom properties (`var(--name)`) into their computed values. Required for email clients that do not support CSS custom properties (most email clients). Variables declared in one `<style>` tag are available in subsequent `<style>` tags.

preserve.description: Keep original custom property declarations (`--name: value`) alongside the resolved values.

encode_entities.description: Encodes special characters (for example, `©`, `™`, and `—`) as their HTML entity equivalents. Improves rendering consistency across email clients with varying character encoding support. Only processes text nodes in the `<body>` and skips `<script>`, `<style>`, `<noscript>`, `<svg>`, and `<head>` elements. Preserves Liquid template tags and avoids double-encoding existing entities.

formatter.description: Controls the output formatting of the final HTML. Only one mode (`prettify` or `minify`) can be active at a time. Set to `"none"` to skip formatting entirely.

minify.description: Options used when `type` is `"minify"`. Reduces file size by stripping whitespace and comments.

line_length_limit.description: Maximum characters per line before inserting a line break.

remove_html_comments.description: HTML comment removal level. `"0"` keeps all comments, `"1"` removes non-conditional comments (preserves MSO conditionals like `<!--[if mso]>`), and `"2"` removes all comments including conditional.

remove_line_breaks.description: Remove all line breaks from the output.

prettify.description: Options used when `type` is `"prettify"`. Produces human-readable, indented HTML output.

indent_size.description: Number of indent characters per level.

wrap_attributes.description: Wrap HTML attributes onto separate lines (`force-expand-multiline` mode).

type.description: Formatting mode to apply.

prevent_widows.description: Replaces the last space in text blocks with a non-breaking space (` `) to prevent a single word from wrapping onto its own line (a “widow”). Only processes text nodes in the `<body>` and skips `<script>`, `<style>`, `<noscript>`, `<svg>`, and `<head>` elements. Preserves Liquid template tags (`{{ }} ` and `{% %}`).

remove_unused_css.description: Scans the HTML and removes any CSS selectors from `<style>` tags that are not referenced in the document. Reduces file size and helps avoid Gmail’s 102 KB clipping limit. HTML and CSS comments are always preserved by this step (comment removal is handled separately by the formatter object).

backend_markers.description: Template syntax delimiters (e.g., Liquid, Handlebars) that the CSS parser should skip over to avoid treating template expressions as invalid CSS.

uglify.description: Shorten (uglify) CSS class names to reduce file size.

whitelist.description:
CSS selectors to always keep, even if they are not found in the HTML.
  - .ReadMsgBody
  - .ExternalClass
  - .aBn
  - .a6S
  - .im
  - .yshortcuts
  - "#outlook"
  - .MsoHyperlink
  - .MsoHyperlinkFollowed

InboxPreviewClient.description: An email client available for inbox previews.

browser.description: Browser used to render the client. Populates when `category` is `Web`.

category.description: Where the client renders. `Mobile` is a phone's native mail app, for example the Gmail App on Android devices. `Application` is a desktop native mail app, for example Apple Mail on macOS. `Web` is webmail viewed in a desktop browser, for example Gmail.com in Firefox, and includes a `browser` value.

client.description: Name of the email client and device.

id.description: Identifier to pass in `client_ids` when you send for an inbox preview.

os.description: Operating system the client runs on. Look for `(Dark Mode)` if you want to locate preview options for dark mode.

InboxPreviewCreditPool.description: Credits available for generating inbox previews.

credits_original.description: Credits originally granted for a tier.

credits_remaining.description: Credits left to spend from this tier.

expires_at.description: When this pool's credits expire, if ever. Expiry is set per pool, not per tier—a purchased pool typically doesn't expire, but a free pool support granted can carry an expiration date. The monthly allowance's `expires_at` also reads `null` when Customer.io can't resolve your current billing period; that's a transient read issue, not a sign the allowance never expires.

tier.description: The credit tier this pool belongs to. The [`free` tier](/accounts/billing/inbox-previews/) covers two kinds of pools, the monthly allowance of 25 credits every account gets and any free pools Customer.io support has granted. Because of that, `free` can appear more than once in the response. The `paid` tier covers credits purchased for the account.

type.description:
Why this device has no screenshot:
  - `bounced`: the vendor rendered the device and reported a bounce.
  - `vendor_timeout`: submitted to the vendor, but didn't finish in time.
  - `client_rejected`: the vendor refused the device id.
  - `vendor_request`: the submission to the vendor itself failed.
  - `abandoned`: submitted, but the outcome is unknown.
  - `expired`: the screenshot rendered successfully but has since aged out of its retention window and is no longer available. Unlike the other types, this isn't a render failure.
  - `other`: any other cause.

A tile with any of these types (except `expired`) was refunded its credit.

total_previews_bounced.description: Previews that produced no screenshot, whether the vendor bounced them or they failed on Customer.io's side. Their credits are refunded when the run settles.

total_previews_cached.description: Previews served from an earlier run's screenshot. Not charged, and not counted in `total_previews_succeeded`.

total_previews_ready.description: How many previews show a screenshot you can fetch, counted from the tiles themselves. This is the progress count to compare against `total_previews_requested`—`total_previews_succeeded` alone reads `0` on a fully cached run. It isn't the completion signal; `is_processed` is. Because a tile can be served by an earlier screenshot of the same content while this run's own render is still in flight, this can reach `total_previews_requested` before the run finishes.

total_previews_requested.description: Previews requested in the job, for the email in the path. On a settled run, this is normally `total_previews_cached` + `total_previews_succeeded` + `total_previews_bounced`.

total_previews_succeeded.description: Previews this run generated itself, excluding cached ones. A fully cached run reports `0` here even though every tile is `Complete`—compare `total_previews_ready` against `total_previews_requested` instead to track progress.

is_processed.description: `true` once every device of every counted node has settled. Under a `node_id` filter, "counted" means the matched nodes only.

node_count.description: How many email nodes the run covers—more than one for a multi-language run. Under a `node_id` filter, how many of them matched.
